stories.headline: Donald Trump Vows to Claim Strait of Hormuz as US Territory Amid Escalating War
stories.body:
United States President Donald Trump has stated at a rally in Garden City, New York, that he will soon declare the Strait of Hormuz as US territory. Speaking to attendees, Trump claimed that no ships can pass through the US blockade of the strategic waterway unless the United States wants them to. His declaration comes amid an escalating conflict in the region.

Iran immediately rejected the American president's claims regarding the critical shipping route. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain under Iranian control. Furthermore, Iranian officials declared that Tehran will not reopen the waterway unless the United States meets several conditions. These demands include lifting economic sanctions, paying compensation for war damage, and releasing frozen Iranian assets.

The dispute follows the outbreak of military conflict earlier this year. The United States and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. Before the conflict began, the Strait of Hormuz served as a vital global energy route, with one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passing through it.

Efforts to manage the war have faced serious challenges. In June, the United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding to halt military operations during the war. However, violence around the strait has continued. Drone attacks recently struck two oil tankers operated by Abu Dhabi's state-owned oil company, ADNOC, inside the Strait of Hormuz. Following the strikes, the United Arab Emirates accused Iran of committing piracy.

Public support for the military action appears low in the United States. A Quinnipiac University poll released in late July found that 60 percent of US voters oppose American military action against Iran.

stories.headline: Luigi Mangione Pleads Guilty to Federal Stalking Charges in CEO Killing
stories.body:
Luigi Mangione has pleaded guilty in federal court to two charges of stalking UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson with the intent to kill him. Mangione entered the plea without a plea deal. Speaking in court, Mangione stated: 'I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan and he died'.

Thompson was shot and killed on December 4, 2024, outside a Midtown Manhattan hotel that was hosting an investor conference. Mangione was arrested five days after the shooting at a McDonald's restaurant in Altoona, Pennsylvania.

Federal prosecutors stated they will seek a sentence of life in prison at Mangione's sentencing scheduled for December 18. The legal proceedings follow complex courtroom rulings. In September 2025, State Judge Gregory Carro dismissed state terrorism charges. Later, in January 2026, US District Judge Margaret Garnett dismissed federal murder and weapons charges on legal technicalities. Mangione's lawyers have now filed a motion to dismiss separate New York state murder and weapons charges, citing double jeopardy principles.

stories.headline: Wildfires Fuel Mass Evacuations Across Europe Amid Extreme Heat
stories.body:
Massive wildfires driven by heatwaves and extreme drought have burned approximately 500,000 hectares of land across Europe. The fires have threatened towns and forced thousands of people to flee their homes in multiple countries.

In Croatia, a fire near Omis killed one person, injured 40 others, and forced 1,200 people to evacuate. Emergency crews in Greece used boats to evacuate more than 300 people from the coastal town of Siviri as flames approached. In France, authorities evacuated 525 people from the village of Luglon in the Landes region. French officials have also detained 474 people, including 183 minors, on suspicion of starting wildfires since July 1.

In Spain, a wildfire in Huelva burned 31,000 hectares and required the evacuation of 700 residents. A Spanish army unit was deployed to remove the historical remains of three 11th-century Aragonese kings from the San Juan de la Peña monastery to protect them from the advancing blaze. Meanwhile, in western Germany, more than 2,000 people were evacuated from the village of Gey as a forest fire moved toward the area.

stories.headline: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow White House Ballroom Construction
stories.body:
The Trump administration has submitted an emergency petition to the US Supreme Court seeking permission to continue construction on a $400 million White House ballroom. The emergency legal request comes after a federal appeals court stepped in to pause the project.

On August 7, the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled 2-1 to halt above-ground construction of the ballroom, stating that the project required congressional approval. The original lawsuit against the construction was initiated by the National Trust for Historic Preservation after the White House East Wing was demolished.

In response to the administration's emergency petition, Chief Justice John Roberts ordered the plaintiffs challenging the ballroom project to file a formal response by Tuesday. In a Supreme Court filing, US Solicitor General D. John Sauer stated that construction on the project is already 65 percent complete. Sauer added that a crew of 250 workers is currently working on the ballroom 20 hours a day, seven days a week.

stories.headline: American Missionary Kevin Rideout Freed After Nine Months of Captivity in Niger
stories.body:
American missionary pilot Kevin Rideout has been released after being held captive in Niger for more than nine months. Rideout was abducted in the capital city of Niamey on October 21 by three armed individuals. Before his kidnapping, Rideout had worked as a missionary in Niger for 19 years.

Following his release, the Christian non-governmental organization SIM International announced that Rideout is in good health and currently under the care of US officials. Reports also indicate that he was transferred to FBI custody after being freed.

stories.headline: President Droupadi Murmu Addresses Nation on Eve of India's 80th Independence Day
stories.body:
President Droupadi Murmu addressed the nation on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day. During her formal address, the full version of the national song Vande Mataram was played both before and after her speech.

In her message, President Murmu highlighted efforts to reform public testing systems. She stated that the government is taking comprehensive steps to reform the public examination system in order to eliminate unfair practices. The address comes after the Centre enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, on July 31. The law imposes strict penalties for individual exam cheating, including up to 10 years of imprisonment and a fine of ₹50 lakh.

The national celebrations will continue with major events led by top leaders. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead the 80th Independence Day celebrations from the iconic Red Fort.

As part of the holiday honors, several police officers across the country were recognized for their service. Twenty Tamil Nadu police personnel were awarded the President's Medal for Distinguished Service and the Medal for Meritorious Service. Additionally, seventeen Delhi Police personnel were named to receive Independence Day service medals.

stories.headline: Tensions Rise Between India and Pakistan Over Indus Waters Treaty Remarks
stories.body:
A diplomatic dispute has broken out after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif warned that Pakistan's water rights under the Indus Waters Treaty represent a 'red line'.

Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah strongly criticized Sharif's remarks, stating that the Indus Waters Treaty has 'sucked our blood'. Meanwhile, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India's position on the treaty remains completely unchanged.

The dispute follows a severe strain in bilateral relations last year. India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance following an April 22, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam that killed 26 people. In response to that attack, India launched Operation Sindoor, targeting terror infrastructure located in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: India Notifies 40 Questions for Census 2027 Phase 2 Including Caste Data
stories.body:
The Indian government has notified 40 questions for Phase 2 of Census 2027. Phase 2 population enumeration will begin on August 17 in Ladakh as well as snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh.

Under the notified rules, Phase 2 of Census 2027 will record caste as declared by the respondent. This marks the first time in independent India that caste across all communities will be enumerated. India last conducted a comprehensive population count of all caste groups in 1931.

Along with caste, the Census 2027 questionnaire includes several new fields. Enumerators will collect data on the number of bank accounts, place of Covid-19 vaccination, mobile phone number, Aadhaar number, and voter card number.
